metadata.title: Internships for secondary school students in general education (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD paper synthesizes evidence from multiple longitudinal datasets (e.g., LSAY, NEPS, BCS70, ELS, NLSY97) and also reports descriptive participation patterns using OECD PISA 2018/2022 data. For PISA-based descriptive results, analysts typically use the complex survey design and sampling weights provided in the PISA international database; however, this document does not specify which weight variables (e.g., student design weights) were applied in the reported figures. The paper does not provide microdata-level modeling details (e.g., PV estimation procedures, missing-data rules, or replicate-weight variance estimation) for the longitudinal studies, so weighting and uncertainty quantification cannot be verified from the excerpt. For the purposes of interpreting the findings, the key limitation is that the document is a cross-study review rather than a single, fully specified re-analysis with transparent survey-weight and PV/missing-data handling.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a short OECD evidence review that summarizes results from multiple longitudinal studies and descriptive PISA participation patterns, rather than reporting a single student-level predictive model with clearly defined cognitive achievement outcomes. Plausible Values (PV) handling is therefore not applicable to the paper’s own analysis because the excerpt does not describe PV-based achievement modeling or PV estimation procedures. Missing-data handling is not reported because the paper does not present a unified empirical estimation pipeline (imputation/deletion rules) for the longitudinal datasets or for the PISA descriptive analyses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The paper does not describe a single analytic subsample construction. Instead, it reports study-level sample sizes and age ranges for multiple longitudinal datasets (e.g., LSAY, NEPS, BCS70, ELS, Marriott Foundation Bridges programme dataset, NLSY97) and summarizes their findings on internships/work placements and later outcomes. For the PISA 2022 descriptive participation figures, the paper indicates that participation is for students aged 15–16 enrolled in general education, but it does not specify additional inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., grade bands, missingness thresholds, or module completion rules) in the provided excerpt.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD short paper reviews quantitative evidence on how internships/work placements during general secondary education relate to later career development and adult labour-market outcomes. It summarizes longitudinal findings across several countries: in Germany (NEPS), internships of several days in a company and additional voluntary internships are associated with lower NEET likelihood and higher earnings/job satisfaction at later ages; in the UK (BCS70), some placement perceptions (e.g., usefulness for career planning) are linked to higher wages and employment-related outcomes, while other associations are not statistically significant. In the US (ELS and NLSY97-based studies), results are mixed, with some studies showing employment gains and stronger effects for socially disadvantaged groups or young men, and weaker effects at longer follow-up horizons. The paper also uses PISA 2018/2022 to describe how internship participation varies by student characteristics (e.g., gender, performance levels, ESCS quartiles) and notes that participation is largely maintained during the COVID-19 period. Because this is a review rather than a single re-analysis, the excerpt does not provide a unified ML pipeline, PV handling, or missing-data/weighting procedures for the longitudinal estimates.
